academicTarget: Independently choose the larger unit fraction across repeated same-size-whole rounds, shade exactly one fourth of a pre-cut circle, and justify the comparison by the size of one part rather than by the size of the denominator.

allowedConcepts: comparing one part of a 3-part whole with one part of a same-size 4-part whole
shading exactly one of four equal sectors to show one fourth
stating a deciding rule based on part size
allowedRepresentations: pairs of identical-size rectangles or circles already cut into equal parts
one shaded part in the same consistent color used since N1
a pre-cut 4-sector circle where tapping selects exactly one sector
excludedExtensions: any fail timer or forced cutoff on a round
difficultyBoundary.startingSupport: One replayable worked demonstration of the same-whole comparison before the first round, plus a single on-request equality check. Rounds never time out; pacing pressure is presentational only and no answer is ever cut off.
difficultyBoundary.expectedIndependence: Independent across repeated rounds after the single demonstration: no hints required, no reteaching, and the shading item completed without assistance.

items.prompt: Quick round: two rectangles are exactly the same size. One shows 1 of 3 equal parts shaded, the other shows 1 of 4 equal parts shaded. Tap the larger shaded part.

options.label: The shaded part of the rectangle cut into 3 equal parts (1/3)
The shaded part of the rectangle cut into 4 equal parts (1/4)

items.prompt: Quick round: two circles are exactly the same size. One shows 1 of 2 equal parts shaded, the other shows 1 of 4 equal parts shaded. Tap the larger shaded part.

options.label: The shaded part of the circle cut into 2 equal parts (1/2)
The shaded part of the circle cut into 4 equal parts (1/4)

items.prompt: This circle is one whole already cut into 4 equal parts. Shade one fourth of the circle.

response.successDescription: Exactly one of the four equal sectors is shaded, the other three are left unshaded, and the existing equal partition is not altered.

items.prompt: You answered fast. Now explain your rule: when both wholes are the same size, how do you decide whether 1/3 or 1/4 is larger?

rubric: Gives a rule based on part size: more equal parts in the same whole means each part is smaller
Mentions that the two wholes are the same size
Does not decide by which bottom number is bigger
Credit partial if the rule is correct in direction but omits the same-size whole condition

academicPrediction.context: Rapid same-whole comparison route after the N2 explainer: repeated quick selection rounds plus one shading production on a pre-cut circle and one part-size justification.
academicPrediction.horizon: independent performance later in the same session, after teaching, with no reteaching available
predictedErrorPatterns: Reverts to the larger-denominator shortcut on the first quick round and picks 1/4
Gets the 1/2 versus 1/4 round right but the 1/3 versus 1/4 round wrong, because the closer part sizes remove the visual cue
Shades 2 or more sectors on N3B-I3 instead of exactly one
Correct fast selections with an explanation that names only the numerals rather than part size
Responds before inspecting part sizes, producing a fast wrong answer with very low timeToFirstValidActionMs
academicPrediction.intervention: Single replayable worked same-whole comparison demonstration plus one on-request equality check; otherwise independent responding across short rounds with no time cutoff.

catalogDecision.reason: The existing N3B artifact validated and its no-timeout brisk-round structure is retained, but the academic contract is revised: a second comparison round using 1/2 versus 1/4 is added so that stability of the inverse rule can be distinguished from a single lucky pick, and the shading contract now explicitly forbids altering the given partition so the item measures unit-fraction selection rather than partitioning.
